title: Authority inventory, owner fencing, change and handover
implementation_status: locally verified on a Base-mainnet fork
accepted_note: Claude authored and ran this. Self-testing is not independent acceptance.

gate.evidence_kind: REAL pinned Base-mainnet Safe 1.4.1, Zodiac Roles v2.1, Morpho Blue and native USDC on an anvil fork at block 51353212. Nothing mocked; this phase has no adversarial stage.
gate.shared_fixture: test/contracts/HeldForkHarness.sol, extracted from the P02 suite so both phases build the same fixture and cannot drift apart. P02 re-verified at 50 tests after the extraction.

the_claim_under_test: An operator can change limits or replace the runner without losing consumption history or guessing what an interrupted operation did.

authority_inventory.method: Enumerated by exercising each authority against the live fork, not asserted in prose. Every party is either used successfully or shown refused, with the SPECIFIC refusal recorded.

parties.safe_owner: The only party that may activate or fence. A stranger calling either is refused.
parties.runner: Authorizes by EIP-712 signature and cannot call the controller directly (NotExecutor). Holds no Zodiac role.
parties.executor: May call, but cannot authorize: an envelope naming the executor and signed by the runner is refused (BadSignature). Not a module on the Safe.
parties.zodiac_roles: An independent refusal layer the controller cannot talk past. The controller's membership is established by a supply that actually succeeded through Roles -- stronger than a probe, since a non-member could not have moved the funds.
parties.nobody_else: An arbitrary address holds none of the authorities.

refusals_are_distinguished.NoMembership_0xfd8e9f28: runnerA -- an enabled module (from the fixture's isolated condition probes) that holds no role, so it reaches the membership check and fails there.
refusals_are_distinguished.NotAuthorized_0x4a0bfec1: runnerB, the executor and any stranger -- not modules on the Safe at all, so they are turned away one step earlier.
refusals_are_distinguished.why_it_matters: Both mean 'cannot act through Roles', but flattening them to one boolean would have hidden that runnerA holds module standing at all.

authority_inventory.immutability: safe, roles, morpho, token, marketId and lineage are immutable. No party, including the owner, can repoint them after deployment; the only state-changing external functions are activate, fence and the two typed entries.

fencing.stops_work_already_authorized: A signature minted BEFORE the fence cannot execute after it (Paused). This is the realistic case: the operator fences precisely because something is in flight.
fencing.leaves_nothing_ambiguous: The fenced operation's id was never consumed, so its outcome is readable rather than guessable.
fencing.preserves_history: Consumption counters, counts, cooldown timestamps and consumed ids all survive a fence. Fencing is not a reset.
fencing.cannot_be_lifted_casually: Only an owner activation under a NEW epoch lifts a fence. A stranger is refused; re-activating the same epoch is refused (StaleActivation).

change_and_handover.runner_replacement_mid_flight: An operation signed by the outgoing runner is unambiguous in BOTH directions after handover: it cannot execute (WrongEpoch) and it did not execute (id not consumed). The same action may then be reauthorized by the new runner -- a first execution, not a re-execution.
change_and_handover.executed_work_survives: An operation that already executed stays consumed across handover, and the new runner re-signing the same id is refused (OperationConsumed). Consumption carries forward.
change_and_handover.retired_runner_is_fully_retired: Not just for the in-flight operation: three fresh ids signed by the retired runner are all refused (BadSignature).
change_and_handover.limit_change_binds_against_history: A ceiling below existing consumption is refused (CeilingBelowConsumption). A tightened-but-valid ceiling is accepted, and the remaining budget is the NEW ceiling minus what was already spent -- 8,000 ceiling with 5,000 spent leaves 3,000, and the native Roles allowance agrees. A customer cannot be surprised by a budget that silently refills on reconfiguration.
change_and_handover.layers_cannot_drift: A reconfiguration that changes a ceiling without re-syncing the native Roles quota is refused (AllowanceDesynchronised), and a refused reconfiguration changes nothing: still fenced, consumption intact, epoch unchanged.

defects_found_in_my_own_work_this_phase.what: The membership probe hard-coded a NoMembership() selector I had not verified.
defects_found_in_my_own_work_this_phase.effect: Every address read as a role member, so the inventory assertions were passing for the wrong reason.
defects_found_in_my_own_work_this_phase.fix: Selectors are now derived by hashing the signatures and checked against what Roles actually returned on the fork. The probe distinguishes three real outcomes instead of guessing at two.

defects_found_in_my_own_work_this_phase.what: Four tests passed _policy() and _expected() as inline arguments to activate() under vm.prank.
defects_found_in_my_own_work_this_phase.effect: NotOwner() -- _expected() makes external view calls that consume the prank before activate runs. The harness documents this exact trap and I walked into it anyway.
defects_found_in_my_own_work_this_phase.fix: Hoisted into locals before the prank.

defects_found_in_my_own_work_this_phase.what: Handover tests activated policyVersion 2 while the harness envelope carries version 1.
defects_found_in_my_own_work_this_phase.effect: WrongPolicyVersion, masking the assertions that were actually under test.
defects_found_in_my_own_work_this_phase.fix: Runner replacement is tested WITHOUT a policy change, which is the scenario it is about; version changes are covered by the limit-change test.

known_gaps: Owner authority is modelled with vm.prank(safe). The real two-signature 2-of-3 ceremony is exercised in the P02 atomic activation batch and evidenced in P00; it is not re-proven per test here.
Nothing is deployed publicly. Local fork only.

runnerA holds module standing on the Safe as a fixture artifact of the isolated condition probes. It holds no role and cannot act, and the inventory records this rather than hiding it -- but a production deployment should not leave a spare EOA enabled as a module.
completeness: P04 clauses covered: authority inventory, owner fencing, change and handover, all against the real pinned fork. Independent acceptance still pending.
next: P05 the private operator console (V4 forbids substituting a CLI without a versioned product amendment), then P06.
